newsitem.title: USA: US Senate Leader says Barshefsky vote not yet set.
newsitem.headline: US Senate Leader says Barshefsky vote not yet set.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said Monday a vote on Charlene Barshefsky's nomination to the post of U.S. Trade Representative had not yet been set.
Lott met Barshefsky, who is currently acting U.S. Trade Representative, Monday morning. Her nomination must go before the full Senate for approval before she can take up the post.

"It's not set," the Republican from Mississippi said. "We discussed a number of substantive issues...all the way from NAFTA (North American Free Trade Agreement) to China MFN (Most Favored Nation status)," he said.

Barshefsky's nomination has been approved by the Senate Finance Committee, which also approved a waiver of a law prohibiting anyone who represented a foreign government in trade negotiations from serving as U.S. Trade Representative.
Barshefsky had done work for Canadian interests when she was a trade lawyer in private practice.
The waiver must be passed by both the House of Representatives and the Senate.
